name: Greek

directionality.text: The script is written from left to right. The source calls left-to-right writing a Greek innovation.

characteristics.text: Archaic Greek texts do not use spaces.
Ancient Greeks mainly used letters of the alphabet to represent numbers.

relationships.text: An adaptation of the Phoenician alphabet.
Had a strong influence on the development of the Latin, Cyrillic, and Coptic scripts.

limitations: No period or geographic claim is stored, because the sources read do not give one in a form suited to this record.
The direction claim describes the script generally, and it does not cover every early inscription.
Modern Unicode capitals are not epigraphic letter forms.
